body.y: Once upon a time there was a jeweller with the finest tools. He decided to give them to his neighbour, a tinsmith who made buckets and roofs.
body.t: Once upon a time there was a jeweller. He had the finest tools: tweezers, tiny hammers, magnifying glasses. One day he decided to do a good deed and give them to his neighbour, a tinsmith who made buckets and roofs.

steps.text: What do you think the tinsmith answered?

options.t: “Thank you, I'll take them!”
options.r: Many people would answer that way: it's an expensive gift, after all. But the tinsmith politely refused.

options.t: “No, they won't suit me”
options.r: That's exactly what he said. You can't straighten a bucket with fine tweezers.

steps.after: Everyone needs tools for their own work. The best tools of someone else won't help you.

steps.text: Here is your toolbox. For now it is empty. The tools light up when you use them. Let's see which ones turn out to be yours.
A friend is struggling to understand a maths problem. What will you do?
steps.hint: There is no single right answer here. Think about how you would really act.

options.t: I'll help explain it step by step
options.r: It takes a long time, and you didn't make it out for break. But your friend's eyes light up: “Oh, I get it!”

options.t: I'll laugh: it's so easy
options.r: You just wanted to make a joke. But your friend blushed and closed the exercise book. The problem stayed unsolved.

options.t: I'll solve it all for him
options.r: Your friend is very grateful: “You saved me!” But in the test he was lost: he never learned to solve it himself.

options.t: I'll leave, I have my own things to do
options.r: Your things are important too. Your friend went to the teacher and figured it out, though not right away. Maybe next time you will help?

steps.text: A new boy has joined the class. At break he sits alone.
steps.hint: There is no single right answer here. Think about how you would really act.

options.t: I'll go over and invite him to play
options.r: The new boy smiled for the first time that day. It looks like you have a new friend.

options.t: I'll wait until he comes over himself
options.r: He is waiting too, and break is over. Maybe he needs time? The next day he nodded to you himself.

options.t: I'll talk about him with my friends
options.r: You were only guessing where he comes from. But the new boy noticed people looking at him and whispering, and he felt uncomfortable.

options.t: I'll show him around the school
options.r: Now he knows where the dining hall is, the library and the best corner of the playground. And he knows you.

steps.text: The class is preparing a celebration in the sukkah. Decorations are needed.
steps.hint: There is no single right answer here. Think about how you would really act.

options.t: I'll draw a design
options.r: Your design is pinned on the board. Everyone is arguing about what colour the paper chains will be.

options.t: I'll make the paper chains
options.r: Your hands are covered in glue, but your paper chains hold better than anyone's.

options.t: I'll say “I can't do it” and step away
options.r: Honestly saying “I can't” takes courage too. They managed without you. Maybe there is a job you would enjoy?

options.t: I'll hand out tasks to everyone
options.r: Everyone got a job they could manage, though two were hurt that nobody asked them. The sukkah was ready in one evening.

steps.text: In a group project everyone is arguing, and nothing is getting done.
steps.hint: There is no single right answer here. Think about how you would really act.

options.t: I'll suggest a step-by-step plan
options.r: The plan is on the board: who does what and by which day. The argument died down.

options.t: I'll listen to everyone and find common ground
options.r: It turned out everyone wanted almost the same thing, they were just saying it in different words.

options.t: I'll talk louder than everyone
options.r: At last they heard you, and one of your ideas was even taken. But two people were hurt, and the argument got even louder.

options.t: I'll do it all alone
options.r: The project is finished and looks great. But you are worn out, and the others say: “Nobody even asked us.”

steps.text: The notice about the charity fair has the wrong date.
steps.hint: There is no single right answer here. Think about how you would really act.

options.t: I'll notice it and tell the organisers
options.r: The date was corrected. Without you, half the guests would have come on the wrong day.

options.t: I'll keep quiet, it's not my business
options.r: Maybe someone else will notice? Nobody noticed. For some reason there were few guests.

options.t: I'll make fun of it in the group chat
options.r: Someone forwarded your message to the organisers, and the date was corrected. But it was unpleasant for them to read the mockery.

options.t: I'll announce the correct date at assembly
options.r: The whole school heard you. The fair raised a record amount.

steps.text: Grandma is struggling to figure out her new phone.
steps.hint: There is no single right answer here. Think about how you would really act.

options.t: I'll patiently show her step by step
options.r: For the first time Grandma sent photos to her grandchildren all by herself. And she proudly told the neighbours about it.

options.t: I'll say: “But it's so simple!”
options.r: For you it really is simple. But Grandma felt awkward asking again.

options.t: I'll do it all for her
options.r: The photo is sent, Grandma thanks you warmly. And tomorrow she will be waiting for you again.

options.t: I'll draw her a cheat sheet with pictures
options.r: The cheat sheet hangs on the fridge. Grandma calls it “the instructions from my professor.”

steps.text: The bench in the courtyard, where the neighbours love to sit, has broken.
steps.hint: There is no single right answer here. Think about how you would really act.

options.t: I'll fix it together with an adult
options.r: The bench is standing again. The neighbours sit on it and don't know who fixed it. But you know.

options.t: I'll write in the neighbours' group chat
options.r: Ten indignant messages in the chat. One neighbour did call a repairman after all, but they had to wait a week.

options.t: I'll describe the damage precisely to the building manager
options.r: The repairman came two days later: you described everything so precisely that he brought the right parts straight away.

options.t: I'll walk past
options.r: The bench is still broken. Maybe it's just unclear where to start?

steps.text: Your younger brother is afraid to go to a new after-school club.
steps.hint: There is no single right answer here. Think about how you would really act.

options.t: I'll tell him how scared I was the first time
options.r: Your brother breathed out: “You were scared too?” And he went.

options.t: I'll say: “Don't be scared, it's nothing”
options.r: You wanted to encourage him. Your brother went, but he no longer tells you what he is afraid of.

options.t: I'll go with him to the first session
options.r: He held your hand for the first five minutes. And then he forgot you were there.

options.t: I'll make a plan with him: what to say when meeting new people
options.r: With a ready-made phrase, getting to know people isn't scary at all.

steps.kicker: From the life of Rav Ashkenazi
steps.title: Don't give up what you are good at
steps.body:
Eleven years ago Rav Shneor Ashkenazi spent three days a week preparing Torah classes. No payment, no feedback: the recordings had one or two hundred views each. On Pesach he decided he was done with teaching.

During the festival days he came across words that became his motto: “Never stop doing what you are good at.” He went back to his classes. One of them became the basis of this game.

steps.text: The last riddle of the workshop. A lion was caught in a hunter's net. Who saved him?

options.t: Another lion
options.r: A good guess, but a lion can't tear a net with his paws.

options.t: An elephant
options.r: The elephant is strong, but too big for thin ropes.

options.t: A little mouse
options.r: Yes! The little mouse gnawed through the ropes one by one.

steps.after: Rav Ovadia Yosef brought this parable in his books. It doesn't matter whether you are a lion or a mouse. What matters is doing your own work.

steps.text: Every person has their own tools. The main thing is to understand what you need them for.
steps.sub: Look at your toolbox: which tools have lit up?
